annotations.annotation_text: Fraternal archetype "yawn" on page 200 ("Anna Livia Plurabelle"): the opposing sons — Shem the Penman (introvert artist, tree, darkness) and Shaun the Post (extrovert politician, stone, light) — manifest here within the two washerwomen gossiping on opposite banks of the darkening Liffey, 500+ river names woven into the text, metamorphosis into elm and stone. Their Brunonian dialectic of coinciding opposites propels the chapter's conflict during this Age of Gods (closing) phase.
